brief: Goldman's Quinn frames Memory and AI Semiconductor weakness as a Nasdaq headwind: GS's Memory and AI Semiconductor baskets fell 9.3% and 6.7% during October 5-12, partly on China's CXMT reporting "key progress" on a new memory-cell architecture competing with SK Hynix. Nasdaq lost 1.3% over the period versus S&P +0.4%. Leveraged Nasdaq positioning initially looked unconcerned, with Nasdaq's 3-month funding versus Fed Funds richening, but that premium to S&P reversed from its local peak alongside October 12th price weakness. In CFTC data, the 'Other' futures category's gross longs sat at one-year highs in notional terms and as a share of open interest as of October 6th, with positive short-term correlation to Memory and AI Semiconductor performance; the note says this category potentially reduced recently implemented length. Whether this carries over to Asset Manager sentiment is unresolved: Asset Manager gross longs on October 6th showed no significant relationship with either barometer.
